title: BA1/143/2020 of KARAN SINGH Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
First Bail Application No. 143 of 2020
Karan Singh ...Applicant
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand ...Respondent

Advocates: Mrs. Pushpa Joshi, Senior Advocate assisted by Ms. Chetna Latwal, Advocate
for the applicant.
Mr. Sandeep Tandon, Deputy Advocate General alongwith Mrs. Mamta Joshi,
Brief Holder for the State of Uttarakhand.
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J. (Oral)
This Bail Application is heard through Video
Conferencing.
2. The applicant is an accused in an FIR; being FIR No. 63
of 2019, for the commission of offences punishable under Sections
302, 307, 353, 34 of IPC; to be read with Section 3/25 of the Arms
Act and Section 26 of the Forest Act, which was registered at P.S.
Kaldhungi, District Nainital.
3. The learned Senior Counsel Mrs. Pushpa Joshi, for the
applicant has argued that, as far as the present applicant is concerned,
since he is not named in the FIR and no specific role, as such, has
been assigned to him, in commission of the offence, he deserves to be
enlarged on bail. She further claims parity on the ground that co-accused persons, namely, Pramjeet and Sooraj have already been
granted bail by the coordinate benches of this Court in Bail
Application No. 2478 of 2019, Paramjeet Singh Vs. State of
Uttarakhand, by an order dated 12.03.2020 and Bail Application No.
2089 of 2019, Sooraj Vs. State of Uttarakhand. Learned Senior
Counsel for the applicant further submits that since in the narration of
set of facts there is no specific role assigned to the present applicant
for commission of offence, thus he deserves to be released on bail.
4. What is surprising is that in para 9 of the present bail
application, there is specific pleadings raised by the applicant that he

2
has, "got no previous criminal history"
, while on contrary, when the
learned Deputy Advocate General for the State was directed to file his
counter affidavit to the bail application, he had placed on record the
details of the previous criminal history of the applicant by way of
Annexure CA-6, wherein the criminal history of the applicant is
detailed and being shown as under:-

5. In response to it, the argument of learned Senior Counsel
for the applicant is that, the applicant Karan Singh, would still be
entitled for parity, with Paramjeet Singh, the reason being that the
other co-accused, who has been granted bail, namely, Paramjeet, who
has also got previous criminal history has been granted bail by the
coordinate Bench of this Court by an order dated 12.03.2020, hence
the principles of parity would still be attracted.
6. This Court is afraid and is not in agreement to accept that
argument; for the reason being that it's a deliberate misleading fact,
which has been intentionally pleaded by the applicant in his bail
application that he has got no criminal history though apparently, the
fact, which has been revealed from the objection submitted by the
learned Deputy Advocate General for the State it apparently shows
that the applicant is carrying the history of about six previous cases
including the one that of the Gangster Act which is a serious offence
in itself.
7. The learned Senior Counsel for the applicant submits that
even if the applicant has got a criminal history, he would still be
entitled for bail, based on the bail which has already been granted to

3
co-accused, namely Paramjeet Singh, because Paramjeet Singh has
also been shown to be having previous criminal history as per CA-6 to
the counter affidavit.
8. I am of the considered opinion, that under law, there
cannot be a negative parity. Hence, an equivalence of parity based on
criminal history of other co-accused, which cannot be placed on a
common pedestal to derive parity for grant of bail. Secondly, the
aspect of parity would not be attracted in the case of present applicant
for being released on bail for the reason being that if Paramjeet
Singh's order dated 12.03.2020, is taken into consideration, the order
passed by the coordinate Bench of this Court on 12.03.2020, it is
primarily based upon the pleading of the applicant therein, thereto
also to the effect that he has got no criminal history and this aspect of
the pleading that applicant was having no criminal history was
conceded by the then Government Advocate, who was appearing in
the case of Paramjeet Singh, and he made a statement that Paramjeet
is not carrying criminal history and it is under that pretext that the
coordinate Bench of this Court believed the statement of Government
Advocate, and had granted bail to Paramjeet Singh, the order dated
12.03.2020, observes as under :-
"5. The learned counsel appearing for the State opposed the bail
application, however, he fairly concedes that the applicant has no
criminal history; co-accused person has been granted bail by the
Co-ordinate Bench of this High Court; role of the present applicant
is similar as alleged against co-accused, who has been granted bail;
the present applicant is not connected with the recovery of mobile
or motorcycles.
6. The applicant is resident of District Udham Singh Nagar. He has
no criminal history; he is in custody since 06.07.2019. Co-accused,
who has similar role, has been granted bail by the Co-Ordiante
Bench of this High Court."
9. I don't know, nor it is apparent from the records as to
what was the reason for the Government Advocate for making such an
irresponsible statement that Paramjeet Singh, had no criminal history
though he too is carrying a criminal history as would be apparent from

4
Annexure CA-6; to the present bail application which is detailed
hereunder:-

10. Hence, the aspect of parity, merely on the basis of a
concession granted by the Government Advocate in the order dated
12.03.2020, cannot be extracted by the applicant herein, to claim an
equivalence for consideration of the bail application despite criminal
history. Hence, this argument is not accepted. Rather it could be said
that bail application itself is based on misleading and incorrect facts,
pleaded therein, thus deserves rejection, on the ground of concealment
itself.
11. Thirdly, the learned Senior Counsel for the applicant
submits that as far as the present applicant is concerned, there is no
specific role assigned to him in the commission of offence. In
response to it, the learned Government Advocate for the State has
drawn attention of this Court to the statement which was recorded
under Section 164 Cr.P.C., as recorded by Mr. Mahendra Singh, who
was an injured person, wherein he has in para 7 of his statement,
specifically pleaded as under:-

In the said para, Mahendra Singh has submitted that
Lakhwinder, Paramjeet and Karan i.e. the present applicant had
fired and fire of Karan had hit the injured Mahendra Singh.

5
12. In view of the reasons assigned above, this Court is not
inclined to grant bail to the present applicant. Accordingly, the bail
application is hereby rejected.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma.J.)
